title: Molinists: assisting grace only a partial cause
source_text: LXIV. Praeterea qui Molinae Jesuitae Methodum & doctrinam sequuntur, docent gratiam adjuvantem, sive cooperantem non se habere proprie ut causam totalem, respectu actus supernaturalis, sed ut causam partialem duntaxat. Et hoc quia gratia adjuvans, ex eorum sententia, non producit actum supernaturalem, nisi dependenter a Libero arbitrio.
pass_a_gloss: LXIV. Moreover those who follow the Method and doctrine of Molina the Jesuit, teach that helping, or cooperating grace does not hold itself properly as total cause, in respect of the supernatural act, but as partial cause only. And this because helping grace, in their opinion, does not produce the supernatural act, except dependently on Free choice.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXIV. Further, those who follow the method and teaching of the Jesuit Molina hold that assisting or cooperating grace is not, strictly, the total cause of the supernatural act, but only a partial cause.
Their reason is that, in their view, assisting grace produces the supernatural act only in dependence on free choice.

choices.why: Scholastic terms for a cause that produces the whole effect versus one that produces it only together with a co-cause; Molinists made grace and free choice partial causes.
